name: Saint-Cyprien / Canet – Pont des Basses
notes: Kite zone regulated by municipal decree from May to September (marked channel). Waves with SE / thermal; tramontane offshore: experienced riders.

name: Le Barcarès – Les 3 Colonnes
notes: Official kite zone; narrow launch behind the dunes. Waves with marin (SE) and summer thermal; tramontane offshore. Also: Parc des Dosses on the Étang de Leucate for flat water by tramontane (experts).

name: Leucate – Le Goulet
notes: Shallow flat water on the Étang de Leucate below Leucate village; first place the tramontane hits. Helmet and impact vest recommended (shallow).

name: Leucate – Les Coussoules / La Franqui
notes: Famous tramontane spot (Mondial du Vent); the tramontane (NW) is offshore here: experts only. Waves with marin (SE). Summer: kite zones only.

name: Étang de La Palme
notes: Shallow flat-water lagoon, safe by tramontane (onshore at the launch); schools on site. Good for learning.

name: Gruissan – La Vieille Nouvelle
notes: Glassy water by tramontane, which is offshore and strong: experienced riders, drift risk, no lifeguards. Sandy track access (2.15 m height bar). No riding on the Étang de l'Ayrolle. Also: Les Chalets / Grazel (sea side, waves with marin; small Grazel lagoon), Narbonne-Plage 8 km north-east.

name: Sète – Pont-Levis
notes: Étang de Thau reference flat-water spot. Launch from the sandbank safe zone, one kite at a time; tramontane (NW) onshore. Booties (urchins). Also: Marseillan and Mèze on the Étang de Thau; Les 3 Digues on the sea side (summer kite zone).

name: Carnon – Petit Travers
notes: Long wild beach between Carnon and La Grande-Motte; works S to SW. Les Roquilles (Carnon west) is forbidden in summer. Also: La Grande-Motte (Grand Travers / Couchant zones), Maguelone 7 km south-west (summer zone).

name: Le Grau-du-Roi – L'Espiguette
notes: Huge wild beach; works S, SE, SW and NW. Long walk from the car park; crowded in summer. Also: Port-Camargue – Plage Sud (flat by NW / mistral) and Le Boucanet (W waves).

name: Beauduc
notes: Legendary Camargue spot, huge beach and flat bay; mistral and S–SW. Remote: dirt track, vehicles max 2.10 m wide, no cars on the beach. Also: Piémanson 12 km east (long wild beach, S–SW).

name: Port-Saint-Louis – Plage Napoléon
notes: Isolated sand spit (protected area); works SE to SSW. All levels. Also: Carteau 6 km north (closed flat bay, S / SE).

name: Marignane – Le Jaï
notes: 5 km sand strip on the Étang de Berre, one of the windiest places in Provence; mistral (strong, gusty), SE and W thermal. Schools on site.

name: Carro
notes: Experienced riders only: tight rocky launch, big waves and currents. SE side-shore; mistral irregular.

name: Marseille – Pointe Rouge
locate: q:Plage de la Pointe Rouge Marseille
notes: Mistral spot (Pointe Rouge / Bonneveine): advanced riders. Kiting banned on the beaches in summer (about mid-June to mid-September).

name: Six-Fours – Le Brusc
notes: Plage des Charmettes, sheltered from swell by the Embiez islands; SW to NW (mistral). Technical launch (rocks). Kiting banned June–September.

name: Hyères – L'Almanarre
notes: World-famous W / SW spot. Kite zone between beach gates 16 and 21 with marked channel; ride beyond the 300 m buoys. Crowded in summer (15 June–15 Sept rules). Also: Le Mérou (L'Ayguade) for east wind.

name: Fréjus – Saint-Aygulf
notes: Summer: kite zone at the Argens mouth (Base Nature side); late Sept to early June: Saint-Aygulf (Esclamandes) kite zone. Thermal S and E winds.

name: Bonifacio – Piantarella
notes: Shallow flat water behind the sandbank to Piana island; E / NE wind (avoid W). July–August: no room to rig, schools only.

name: Bonifacio – Tonnara
notes: World-renowned W (libeccio) spot in the Ventilègne gulf; flat by east wind. The closed bay of Pont de Ventilègne next door suits beginners. Also: Balistra (wild beach with lagoon, flat by W).

name: Figari – Baie de Figari
notes: Closed, shallow bay, very safe: ideal for beginners. Works with W (thermal, libeccio, mistral). Large kite school.

name: Porto-Pollo – Plage du Taravo
notes: Summer thermal almost every afternoon; kite zone marked by yellow buoys (managed by an association). Good for beginners and foil.

name: Calvi – La Pinède
notes: Big sandy bay; W (libeccio) and NE. Summer: head to the north-east end of the beach, away from swimmers.

name: Lac de Monteynard
notes: Famous thermal spot: strong south wind in spring and summer afternoons, north return wind. Main launches at Treffort.
